1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 0102/2014 registered at Police Station Gandhi Nagar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Padam Kumar Khanna and Investigating Officer (IO), Police Station Gandhi Nagar, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 07.12.2008.
A female child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is stated that due to temperamental differences arose between the parties, they started living separately from each other since 11.06.2013.

On the basis of complaint filed by respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No. 0102/2014 at Police Station Gandhi Nagar, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC was registered against petitioners.
Petitioner no

. 1 and respondent no. 2 vide decree sheet dated Yogesh Arora & Ors vs The State (Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63956907/
1 17.05.2022 by way of mutual consent dissolved their marriage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the pendency of the present FIR, with the intervention of family members and respectable person of the society, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes vide Settlement Deed dated 10.07.2019 before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.

7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement Deed dated 10.07.2019 before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi and learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that affidavit showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs.
Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court has been filed and the same has been taken on record.

8. It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

9. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 3,25,000/- in four instalments in the following manner:
a. First instalment of Rs.1,25,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the first motion petition. b.
Second instalment of Rs.1,25,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the second motion petition.

c.
Third instalment of Rs.75,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 after obtaining the decree of divorce by way of a mutual consent.
d. Fourth/Final instalment of Rs. 75,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs.75,000/- today, i.e., 15.02.2023 by way of two Demand Drafts i.e. DD bearing No.
807896 for a sum of Rs. 35,000/- drawn on UCO Bank, Delhi High Court and DD bearing No.
807895 for a sum of Rs. 40,000/- drawn on UCO Bank, Delhi High Court and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
11.

In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 0102/2014 registered at Police Station Gandhi Nagar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
